chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام.

About buried treasure: how much is due on it? He عليه السلام said: "The khums." And about minerals: how much is due on them? He عليه السلام said: "The khums." Likewise, lead, brass, and iron, and everything that is from the minerals—there is taken from them what is taken from gold and silver.

key_terms.الذَّهَبِ: gold, used as a legal benchmark for assessment
key_terms.الرَّصَاصُ: lead as one example of mineral wealth
key_terms.الصُّفْرُ: brass or yellow copper alloy mentioned among minerals
key_terms.الْحَدِيدُ: iron as a mineral subject to the same ruling
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth tax due on specified forms of wealth
key_terms.الْفِضَّةِ: silver, used as a legal benchmark for assessment
key_terms.الْكَنْزِ: buried treasure or hidden wealth discovered
key_terms.الْمَعَادِنِ: minerals or mined natural resources extracted from the earth

ai.seo_question: How much khums is due on treasure and minerals in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that khums is due on buried treasure and on extracted minerals. It also clarifies that this ruling applies broadly to mineral resources such as lead, brass, and iron, treating them under the same legal principle as gold and silver.
